media.alt: Health care gets a boost in East Africa

content.text: The Aga Khan University's health programme in Arusha, Tanzania got a boost on Wednesday, July 18, 2012, with the announcement by the German government of financial support to the tune of € 10 million for the University's health programme in Arusha, Tanzania.

The agreement which was signed by representatives of the governments of the Federal Republic of Germany and the East African Community (EAC) will see the allocation of funds for various aspects of the project. This includes the construction and renovation of two university buildings, a student dormitory as well as improving course material for nurse and midwife education. New study and job training programmes in rural areas, practical short courses, scholarships and funding new research will also be part of the programme.

The overall €33 million project will be implemented through a trilateral agreement between the Aga Khan Development Network, KFW Development Bank (Germany) and the EAC. The programme is aimed primarily at disadvantaged and medically poorly supplied regions in East Africa. It is envisioned that the infrastructural and qualitative expansion of health care systems will make a significant contribution to improving the health of the regional population.
